title: Must Friends and Kindred Drop and Die
description: Must Friends and Kindred Drop and Die in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 47, headed “[Supplement.] Death of kindred improved”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Must friends and kin-dred drop and die? And help-ers be with-drawn? While sor-row with a weep-ing eye Counts up our com-forts gone?

lines: Must friends and kindred drop and die?
While sorrow with a weeping eye
Be thou our comfort, mighty God!
Nor leave us in this dangerous road,
O may our feet pursue the way
With love and holy zeal obey
Let us be wean'd from all below,
While death invites our souls to go

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
